We'll come up with a plan and then let's rub it together next week' reads as WagerTech accepting Kobi's offer and taking the plan (ledger L0919 owner = 'likely WagerTech'; L1530 later confirms WagerTech owns the rollout plan). The remaining gap is small: Jumpr's offer of training sessions/office hours/launch-day help is not tracked, and epic WAGR-22 'Training, Enablement & Admin Handoff' exists but is empty.
q1: Found verbatim. Re-fetched doc 1NwBfx21p4Y0Vd04q67s2NgssudX_-XnjuktiXh0JreI (text/html, converted with gdoc_html2txt.py); whitespace-normalized quote matches exactly, including the 'uh', at 00:52:37.
q2: Partially supports. Context (00:49:17-00:54:46): Kobi asks WagerTech about their go-live and training plans ('I just want to talk about go live a little bit too and your plans around training'), recommends a transition plan and office hours, then offers: 'things like training sessions, office hours, if you want to consider us helping with, we can do that.' The next words 'Okay. Awesome. We'll come up with a plan and then let's rub it together next week' are most likely the client's reply. All 174 speaker turns in the doc are labelled Kobi Kunasekaran, so speaker attribution cannot be trusted. The ledger row L0919 records owner as 'Unclear from diarization (likely WagerTech, with Jumpr offering help)'. Earlier at 00:51:25 the transition plan was framed as WagerTech's work ('We can work on that for sure'; L0916 owner 'WagerTech (with Jumpr input)'). The claim that 'Jumpr agreed to draft' the plan is not supported; at most Jumpr offered help and agreed to review it together.
q3: No later meeting shows a joint training/go-live plan review. The 2026-07-15 weekly sync (the 'next week') has no plan review, only an action for Emily to watch the training video. L1530 (2026-08-04): Emily says WagerTech committed to a clearer rollout plan; that confirms WagerTech owns the rollout plan. Later Jumpr delivered training material: L1580/L1581/L1582 (2026-08-06, Taryn's rep training doc, Kobi to review), L1583 (training videos deferred until build is near complete), L1707 (2026-08-11, living user-facing training manual to hand to the client), L1709 (admin user manual), L2183 (2026-08-31, written handover doc), L3042 (2026-09-24, Loom walkthroughs). These do not resolve a 'go-live/training plan', but they weaken the 'no later evidence of delivery' part of the claim.
q4: No ticket for a training plan, office hours, super-user training or launch day. JQL text search (training OR go-live OR rollout OR office hours OR enablement) returned only build/CMS tickets; summary search returned WAGR-22 'Training, Enablement & Admin Handoff' (Epic, Open, unassigned, due 2026-08-14, no description, 0 comments), WAGR-18 'Deployment & Go Live Prep' (Epic, Open, 0 comments), WAGR-23 'Milestone: Phase 1 Go-Live' (Open, 2 comments; the 2026-08-10 comment tracks WagerTech's outstanding rollout-plan commitment), WAGR-26 'Post Go Live Support', WAGR-479 'Go Live Tasks' (Epic, Open, 0 comments, created 2026-09-29, for non-build go-live items). parent in (WAGR-22, WAGR-18, WAGR-479) returned no children; 'office hours'/'super user'/'training plan' text search returned only WAGR-438 and WAGR-393 (unrelated). So the topic is covered only at an empty epic level (WAGR-22).
corrections: Owner of the 'come up with a plan' action is most likely WagerTech, not Jumpr (diarization assigns every line to Kobi). Jumpr's part was an offer to help with training sessions/office hours and to review the plan together.
Training documentation was delivered later by Jumpr (L1580-L1583, L1707, L1709, L2183); the gap is the go-live/training plan and the office-hours/launch-day offer, not training material in general.
Best home for any follow-up: WAGR-22 (Training, Enablement & Admin Handoff epic, empty) or WAGR-479 (Go Live Tasks), linked to WAGR-23.
